evasive

/ih-VAY-siv/ - the stress falls on VAY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Evasive means avoiding a direct answer or commitment.

Asked how the driving test had gone, Lena turned evasive and offered a detailed report on the weather instead.

Example

Asked why he had left his last job, Marcus praised the town, the office plants, and 'the journey of growth itself.' The interviewer tried twice more, then wrote a single word in the margin: evasive. He had spoken for three minutes without answering anything.

Evasive is more exact than 'vague' because vagueness can be accidental—a fuzzy memory, a clumsy explanation—while an evasive answer is steered away from the question on purpose.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

cagey: Cagey means wary and reluctant to give anything away — the caution of someone protecting an advantage, volunteering nothing. Evasive is more active: when a direct question lands, the evasive speaker steers around it. Cagey holds back; evasive dodges.

noncommittal: Noncommittal means refusing to take a side or make a promise — 'we'll see' is the classic noncommittal answer — and it need not hide any facts. Evasive is about the question itself: an evasive reply supplies plenty of words while avoiding the answer that was asked for.

slippery: Slippery is the informal word for a person you can never pin down — one who slides out of your grip like wet soap — and it judges the whole character. Evasive describes behavior in the moment: answers that go around a direct question instead of through it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

direct: answering the question that was asked, plainly

forthcoming: readily offering information without being pressed

Where it sits · how fully the question goes unanswered — guarded → evasive → stonewalling

guarded vs. evasive: A guarded witness still answers, just carefully and without volunteering extras; an evasive one steers around the question itself.

stonewalling vs. evasive: Stonewalling passes evasive on the same road: the evasive speaker dodges and deflects, while the stonewaller simply refuses to engage at all, question after question.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out (a form of ex-)

Root — vas

Root — vas: to go

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: tending to

Put it together

Put it together: E- (out) + vas (to go) + -ive (tending to) = tending to go out of the way. Latin evadere meant to escape—literally to go out—and evasive keeps the escape artist's spirit: the evasive answer slips out of the question's grasp and leaves the asker holding air.

Use the root in a new word: invade

Use the root in a new word: invade: Every June the ants invade the pantry, and no trap we set has ever slowed them down.

Word Choice

neutral

Evasive describes dodging under questioning—answers that go around instead of through. A secretive person (another word in this unit) hides things as a standing habit even when no one asks, and to conceal is to hide one particular thing; evasive is what someone becomes the moment a direct question lands and slides off.
